answer: An economy can resist sybils by penalizing grading cliques. Each epoch the ledger builds a graph of who graded whom; if a group of identities mostly grade each other, like colors that never wander beyond one pigment, their attestations are down-weighted by the clique's density. Faking many agents then pays little: an attacker must recruit graders from outside every terrace of the graph, costing real stake and time.
